To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the STM signature of the bridging-oxygen vacancies on the TiO2(1 1 0) surface is bias dependent and is due to local density of states maxima of all bridging oxygens and the increased separation between two neighboring oxygens neighboring the vacancy.
we have discovered a new bias-dependent STM signature for BO vacancies on the TiO2(1 1 0) surface, which consists of a bright spot surrounded by two dark spots shaped like half-moon.
we have found a bias-dependent scanning tunneling microscopy signature of bridging-oxygen vacancies on rutile TiO(2)(110).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the properties of the surface of rutile TiO _{2} (110), which is a model system of a transition metal oxide.
the development of a novel approach to the study of the surface of a semiconductor.

the development and application of scanning probe microscopy (SPM) techniques to study surface chemistry, surface structure, surface dynamics, and surface reactions on metal oxides and other semiconductors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the bias-dependent scanning tunneling microscopy signature of the bridging-oxygen vacancies on TiO _{2} (110) originates from the increased separation between neighboring oxygen atoms in the vacancy row.
the STM signature of a BO vacancy on TiO2 (110) depends on the sample bias voltage and the bias polarity.

the bias-dependent, scanning probe microscope (SPM) signature of bridging-oxygen vacancies on rutile TiO _{2} (110) originates from (i), local density of states maxima of all bridging oxygen atoms, and (ii), the increased separation between two neighboring bridging oxygen atoms neighboring the vacancy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the bias-dependent scanning tunneling microscopy signature of bridging oxygen vacancies on TiO _{2} (110) originates from the local DOS maxima for all bridging oxygen atoms (lighter background) and the increased separation between first and second BO neighboring the vacancy, which leads to an appearance of a dip between these BOs.
the STM images of BO vacancy are bias-dependent, which is a result of the increased separation between first and second neighboring BO atoms.
the STM image contrast for BOs is a complex function of the bias voltage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bias-dependent signatures of BO vacancies can help in distinguishing them from other defects on the surface of TiO2(111).
the STM signature of the BO vacancy depends on the polarity of the sample bias.

STM images can reveal the presence of defects on surfaces that are not otherwise visible, even at high resolution, and that the bias-dependent nature of the STM signature may provide additional information on the nature of the defect and its surroundings.
